  1. Serving runtimes

Serving runtimes

A ClusterServingRuntime is a cluster-scoped template that says which container image serves a model format. Entries in models select one by name.

llmInferenceServices entries do not use runtimes. They define their container directly. See LLM inference services.

Runtimes installed by default

With default values the chart installs 16 cluster-scoped runtimes: 14 from upstream KServe and 2 added by this chart.

Runtime name Serves Typical hardware Source
kserve-openvino OpenVINO IR, ONNX, TensorFlow, Hugging Face text generation CPU This chart
kserve-vllm-cpu Hugging Face causal LLMs CPU This chart
kserve-vllmserver Hugging Face causal LLMs GPU Upstream
kserve-huggingfaceserver Hugging Face transformers, encoders, embeddings, generation CPU or GPU Upstream
kserve-huggingfaceserver-multinode Large Hugging Face models across nodes Multi-GPU Upstream
kserve-tritonserver TensorRT, ONNX, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Python backends CPU or GPU Upstream
kserve-tensorflow-serving TensorFlow SavedModel CPU or GPU Upstream
kserve-torchserve PyTorch .mar archives CPU or GPU Upstream
kserve-sklearnserver scikit-learn (joblib, pickle) CPU Upstream
kserve-xgbserver XGBoost CPU Upstream
kserve-lgbserver LightGBM CPU Upstream
kserve-pmmlserver PMML CPU Upstream
kserve-paddleserver PaddlePaddle CPU Upstream
kserve-autogluonserver AutoGluon CPU Upstream
kserve-mlserver Seldon MLServer: scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, MLflow CPU Upstream
kserve-predictiveserver KServe predictive server CPU Upstream

List them in a live cluster:

kubectl get clusterservingruntime

Inspect exactly which model formats a runtime advertises, including versions and priorities:

kubectl get clusterservingruntime kserve-huggingfaceserver -o yaml

The authoritative list of supported modelFormat values is always the live cluster object. Use the command above rather than assuming a format is supported.

Choosing a runtime 

flowchart TD
    A[Model artifact] --> B{Generative LLM?}
    B -- Yes --> C{GPU available?}
    C -- Yes --> D[kserve-vllmserver<br/>or llmInferenceServices]
    C -- No --> E[kserve-vllm-cpu<br/>or kserve-openvino]
    B -- No --> F{Framework}
    F -- scikit-learn --> G[kserve-sklearnserver]
    F -- XGBoost --> H[kserve-xgbserver]
    F -- LightGBM --> I[kserve-lgbserver]
    F -- PyTorch --> J[kserve-torchserve]
    F -- TensorFlow --> K[kserve-tensorflow-serving]
    F -- ONNX / TensorRT --> L[kserve-tritonserver<br/>or kserve-openvino]
    F -- Transformers --> M[kserve-huggingfaceserver]

Selecting a runtime for a model 

models:
  - name: fraud-detector
    runtime: kserve-sklearnserver
    modelFormat: sklearn
    storageUri: s3://models/fraud/v3

If you omit runtime, modelDefaults.runtime applies. If you omit modelFormat, modelDefaults.modelFormat applies.

runtime and modelFormat must be compatible. A runtime rejects a format it does not advertise, and the InferenceService stays unready with a runtime resolution error.

Enabling and disabling built-in runtimes

Upstream runtimes are controlled per runtime under kserve-runtime-configs. Note the key is disabled, not enabled.

kserve-runtime-configs:
  kserve:
    servingruntime:
      enabled: true
      tritonserver:
        disabled: true
      torchserve:
        disabled: true
      paddleserver:
        disabled: true

Disable every upstream runtime at once:

kserve-runtime-configs:
  kserve:
    servingruntime:
      enabled: false

Available runtime keys:

tensorflow, mlserver, sklearnserver, xgbserver, huggingfaceserver, huggingfaceserver_multinode, tritonserver, pmmlserver, predictiveserver, paddleserver, lgbserver, torchserve, autogluonserver, vllmserver

Overriding runtime images

Useful for private registries, air-gapped clusters, and version pinning.

kserve-runtime-configs:
  kserve:
    servingruntime:
      huggingfaceserver:
        image: registry.example.com/mirror/kserve/huggingfaceserver
        tag: v0.20.0
        imagePullSecrets:
          - name: registry-credentials
      vllmserver:
        image: registry.example.com/mirror/vllm/vllm-openai
        tag: v0.11.0

The chart’s CPU runtimes

OpenVINO

Efficient CPU inference for OpenVINO IR, ONNX, and TensorFlow models, and the default for modelDefaults.runtime.

clusterServingRuntimes:
  openVINO:
    enabled: true
    name: kserve-openvino
    image: openvino/model_server:2026.3
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: "2"
        memory: 4Gi
      limits:
        cpu: "4"
        memory: 8Gi

The resources here are the runtime template defaults. Per-model resources override them.

vLLM on CPU

Generative inference without a GPU. Use it for development, tests, and small models.

clusterServingRuntimes:
  vllmCPU:
    enabled: true
    name: kserve-vllm-cpu
    image: public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-cpu-release-repo:v0.26.0
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    maxModelLen: 8192
    gpuMemoryUtilization: "0.7"
    shmSize: 2Gi
Key Meaning
maxModelLen Maximum context length, passed as --max-model-len
gpuMemoryUtilization Passed as --gpu-memory-utilization; vLLM requires it even in CPU mode
shmSize Size of the /dev/shm volume; raise it if vLLM reports shared memory errors

CPU generation is slow. Expect seconds per token for multi-billion-parameter models. Use small models on CPU and reserve large models for GPU.

Disable either runtime when you do not need it:

clusterServingRuntimes:
  openVINO:
    enabled: false
  vllmCPU:
    enabled: false

Adding your own runtime

The chart does not template arbitrary runtimes. Apply a custom ClusterServingRuntime separately and reference it by name:

apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterServingRuntime
metadata:
  name: my-custom-runtime
spec:
  supportedModelFormats:
    - name: my-format
      autoSelect: true
  containers:
    - name: kserve-container
      image: registry.example.com/my-runtime:1.0.0
      args:
        - --model_path=/mnt/models

models:
  - name: custom-model
    runtime: my-custom-runtime
    modelFormat: my-format
    storageUri: s3://models/custom/v1
